turns.doctor_question: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, I guess I'm here because my mind just won't stop. It's like I'm constantly jumping from one worry to the next. Lately, I've been obsessing over whether our lab's new partnership is going to mean my position gets cut. And then I start thinking about whether my data are wrong, which leads to worrying about my bills piling up. Then I stress about my family thinking I'm falling behind, and... I don't know, whether I've already completely ruined my chances at getting into grad school. It's just all the time.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient describes persistent, pervasive worry across multiple domains (job security, data errors, personal finances, family perceptions, and future grad school prospects) occurring all the time.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you been experiencing this constant worrying across different areas of your life—has it been going on for more than six months, or did it start more recently?
turns.patient_response: It's been going on for a while now... definitely more than six months. I'd say it's been about seven months. It started right around the time our lab had this big funding shift, and they brought in a commercial partnership. That just changed how everything was being run, and I guess my mind just hasn't stopped spinning since then.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient confirms experiencing persistent worrying for about seven months, noting that their mind hasn't stopped spinning since a major lab change.

turns.doctor_question: Along with all this worrying, have you noticed physical symptoms like feeling restless or on edge, muscle tension, fatigue, or trouble sleeping nearly every day?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, definitely. At work, I just feel really wound up... like I can't even settle into my chair. I end up constantly tapping my foot or checking my messages. Sometimes I catch myself just walking back to the instrument room for no actual reason, just because I can't sit still. And I guess I am pretty on edge, because even just normal lab noises have been completely startling me lately.

symptom_reasoning.S058: The patient explicitly confirms feeling wound up, unable to sit still or settle into their chair, and persistently on edge.

turns.doctor_question: Would you say your worrying happens even about things that have nothing to do with the lab situation, or does it mostly stay focused on issues connected to that change at work?
turns.patient_response: It definitely spills over into everything. Um, it's not just the lab. Like I mentioned earlier, it's my bills, my family... everything. I try to stop it, I really do. I'll tell myself to just focus on one task, like finishing a report or checking an assay. But... it just doesn't work. One worry sets off another, and pretty soon I'm just staring at the screen while my head is running through every possible way things could go wrong.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient reports that worry is not confined to work but spills over into multiple life domains, including bills and family, indicating generalized worry.
symptom_reasoning.S057: The patient describes trying unsuccessfully to stop worrying, noting that one worry triggers another and they are unable to halt the process.
